newsitem.title: UK: UK air passenger traffic up 5.0 percent in '96 - CAA.
newsitem.headline: UK air passenger traffic up 5.0 percent in '96 - CAA.

text.p: Britain's airports handled five percent more air traffic last year, the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) said on Monday.

Announcing its latest annual statistical report, the CAA said that passenger numbers rose to 135.998 million, with international traffic rising to 105.549 million passengers from 101.592 million in 1995.
Total aircraft movements also rose five percent, to 1.69 million take-offs and landings last year.

But the report said that punctuality deteriorated, with average delays increasing by two minutes to 14 minutes. Average delays on scheduled services increased to 11 minutes from nine in 1995, while delays on charter flights increased by three minutes to 36 minutes.

It said the statistics did not analyse the causes of the delays, which could include weather, industrial action, air traffic control problems and aircraft breakdowns, as well as missing passengers and security hold-ups.
Meanwhile, the report said that competition from the Channel Tunnel railway operated by Eurotunnel continued to take traffic away from airlines.

Passenger traffic on air routes between the UK and France fell by three percent last year, with London-Paris traffic down 12 percent. It said that since the Eurostar inter-city rail service began two years ago annual London-Paris air traffic had fallen by more than 25 percent, or one million passengers.
